tone_statements.citation: Acheampong, Samuel Owoahene. 2024. The syntax of Likpakpaanl elliptical constructions. Doctoral thesis, Goethe-Universität Frankfurt am Main. doi:10.21248/gups.87836; urn:nbn:de:hebis:30:3-878365
tone_statements.quote: Likpakpaanl has three level tones: low (ˋ ), high (ˊ ) and mid (ˉ) (Steele & Weed 1966). There is also a contour tone of a convex pattern in non-identical adjacent vowel strings (Bisilki 2021). The syllable is the tone bearing unit and can be a vowel or a syllabic nasal. Tone has both lexical (9) and grammatical functions in the language. The grammatical function of tone is shown shortly in the tense-aspect properties of Likpakpaanl following later in this section
tone_statements.summary: 3 level tones L, H, M + convex contour on non-identical VV; TBU syllable; lexical and grammatical (aspect) tone.

tone_statements.citation: Bisilki, Kwesi Abraham. 2023. The causative construction in Likpakpaanl (Konkomba) [running title: Causative constructions in Likpakpaanl (Konkomba) from an areal-typological perspective]. Studies in African Linguistics 52(1-2): 189-213. doi:10.32473/sal.52.1and2.132707
tone_statements.quote: Three level tones (high, mid, and low) are identified in the tonal system of Likpakpaln. The syllable is the tone‑bearing unit in Likpakpaln and can be a vowel or a syllabic nasal. Each member of a vowel sequence (VV) in a syllable receives a separate tone marking as notational convention. ... the involvement of the M tone phenomenon in lexical distinctions in Likpakpaln is far less elaborate compared to the role of the high and low tones. ... Beyond the three tone levels, downstep has also been reported in Likpakpaln (Schwarz, 2007). This phenomenon is particularly evident in focus contexts, especially in responses to questions.
tone_statements.locator: p. 23 of 37, §3.5.1 'Tone Inventories' (conclusion restated p. 26, §3.5.2 end: 'a three‑way level tone system operates in the language, with the tonemes being high, mid, and low')
tone_statements.summary: 3 level tones H, M, L (M marginal lexically) + downstepped H; TBU syllable; no phonological contour tones (HL on non-identical VV only); lexical and grammatical tone (pronouns, aspect).

sources.citation: Adouna, Gbandi. 2009. Description phonologique et grammaticale du konkomba, langue Gur (voltaïque) du Togo et du Ghana – parler de Nawaré. Thèse de doctorat, Université Rennes 2 (cotutelle Université de Lomé). 399 pp. HAL tel-00416375.
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: open copy online
sources.note: Full phonology part (phonemes, syllable, tones). Silent on word stress: the language is treated as a tone language with three phonological tones H/M/B (p. 91), tones on an autonomous tonal tier in a CV open-syllable language (pp. 99-101); no section on accent/stress. The only 'accent' remark is utterance-level and hedged: 'On pourrait parler d'un accent d'intensité qui distingue les deux énoncés' (p. 185, appellative vs. praise-exclamation), not word stress.

sources.note: Brief sketch §1.1 'Tone system' (p. 118): 'While it is clear that Konkomba is a tone language, further information about its features is urgently required'; possibly three tonemes H/M/L (Abbott & Steele 1973) vs. H/L plus downstep (Steele 1977 Data Sheets); minimal pair up̀i 'woman' vs. upí 'sheep'. Nothing on stress.
